feature: Measurements named for their mode, one set of caliper controls
summary: A Gap lands as a layer called Gap 16 and a Distance as Distance 124 (a Size is still Size 124 × 30). Any caliper, including a whole Size measurement, shows the same Role, Caliper, Thickness and Chip rows in the same place, and a colour you pick there sticks and is used for the next measurement.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/measurements-named-for-their-mode-walk.json.

try.do: Open a screenshot, press I, and make one Gap, one Size and one Distance measurement.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Read the Layers list (Gap 16, Size 124 × 30, Distance 124) and the Measurements list (Gap, Size, Distance).
Click the Size row in Layers: Appearance shows Role, Caliper, Thickness and Chip.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Caliper colour well and pick a colour: both of the Size measurement's calipers change.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open the Size group and click Height: no Arrange section, the Caliper row sits where it does for a Gap.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Command-click the Gap, Size and Distance rows: Caliper reads Mixed and no Role is lit; pick one colour and all three take it.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Measure another button in Size mode: it comes out in the colour you just gave.

evaluate: Is 'Gap 16' / 'Distance 124' in Layers, with just 'Gap' / 'Distance' in Measurements (the number beside it), the naming you wanted?
Picking a whole Size measurement now shows its calipers' colours; is that where you looked for them, or did you expect to open the group first?
With several calipers picked, does Caliper reading Mixed and the Role row with nothing lit read clearly to you?
Should a colour change on one Size caliper also become the colour for the next Distance, or only the next Size (today it follows the role)?
rough: On a small window the Chip rows still sit below the fold of Appearance's own scroller for every caliper, the same as before; the Caliper row itself is on screen. That is the dock's rule that Appearance scrolls inside itself (your call on 2026-09-20, 'Guarantee the fold').

The redline mock names rows by element ('Save Changes · width') and shows one Color row in a Measurement section; the app names them by mode and puts the look in Appearance's part rows. Both follow your later answers: the look moved into Appearance on your call on 2026-09-09, and names by mode are your call on 2026-10-13.
A picked Size measurement keeps a Corner Radius row at the end of Appearance, which rounds its Box. Masked by is gone from it, the way a caliper never had one.
Old documents and the Current release keep the name Measure: only measurements made where Size is a group record their mode.
